tests.title: PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is read fresh for each push rather than cached across pushes
given: a registered active patch branch patch/foo
tests.when: two successive pushes to patch/foo are made, the first with PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN="true" and the second with the variable changed to "false" in between
then: the first push forwards and is accepted
the second push is rejected with the fork-push message
GetVariableFunc is invoked once per push rather than reused from a previously read value
tests.pseudocode: setVar('PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN','true'); p1=push(patchFoo); assert p1.status=='ok'; setVar('PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN','false'); p2=push(patchFoo); assert p2.status=='ng'

tests.title: Only the exact string "true" enables PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN
given: a registered active patch branch patch/foo
tests.when: for any string value other than the exact literal "true" (unset, empty string, "TRUE", "1", "false", "true " with trailing space)
then: PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is treated as disabled and the origin-mode refusal path (04-REQ-3) is taken instead of forwarding
tests.pseudocode: for v in gen_non_true_strings(): setVar('PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN', v); r=push(patchFoo); assert r.status=='ng'

tests.title: A variable-store error reading PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is treated as disabled without surfacing the store error to the client
given: GetVariableFunc configured to return an error when reading PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN
tests.when: a push to the registered patch branch patch/foo is made
then: the ref is rejected with the standard 'branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url> instead' message
the raw report-status response contains no store-error text or stack trace
tests.pseudocode: getVar=errFunc; r=push(patchFoo); assert r.message=='branch is synced from origin; push to '+gitURL+' instead'; assert !contains(r.raw, storeErrText)

tests.title: A refs/heads update to a non-deleted registered patch branch that is not the integration branch and not a delete is classified as a guard candidate
given: a patches row with branch_name=patch/foo and status=active
tests.when: the classifier evaluates a push command Name=refs/heads/patch/foo, New=<nonzero sha>
then: the command is classified as a guard candidate
tests.pseudocode: cmd={Name:'refs/heads/patch/foo', New: sha1}; assert classifyCandidate(ws, patches, cmd) == true

tests.title: A tag ref update is excluded from guard candidacy without querying the patches table
tests.when: the classifier evaluates a push command Name=refs/tags/v1, New=<nonzero sha>
then: the command is not a guard candidate
no patches table query is issued for this command
tests.pseudocode: cmd={Name:'refs/tags/v1', New:sha1}; spyDB=countingDB(); classifyCandidate(ws, spyDB, cmd); assert spyDB.queryCount==0

tests.title: The integration branch is never a guard candidate even when a patches row shares its name
given: a patches row with branch_name=main and status=active
tests.when: the classifier evaluates a push command Name=refs/heads/main, New=<nonzero sha>
then: the command is not classified as a guard candidate
tests.pseudocode: cmd={Name:'refs/heads/main', New:sha1}; assert classifyCandidate(ws, patches, cmd)==false

tests.title: A branch matching a soft-deleted patches row is excluded from guard candidacy
given: a patches row with branch_name=patch/gone and status=deleted
tests.when: the classifier evaluates a push command Name=refs/heads/patch/gone, New=<nonzero sha>
then: the command is not classified as a guard candidate
tests.pseudocode: cmd={Name:'refs/heads/patch/gone', New:sha1}; assert classifyCandidate(ws, patches, cmd)==false

tests.title: A delete update to a registered patch branch is excluded from guard candidacy and accepted as a delete
given: a patches row with branch_name=patch/foo and status=active
tests.when: a push contains command Name=refs/heads/patch/foo, New=zero hash (a delete)
then: the command is not classified as a guard candidate
the delete is applied exactly as before this spec
tests.pseudocode: cmd={Name:'refs/heads/patch/foo', New: zeroHash}; assert classifyCandidate(ws, patches, cmd)==false; r=push([cmd]); assert r.status=='ok'; assert refDeleted('patch/foo')

tests.title: A direct push to a fork-synced patch branch is rejected per-ref leaving the local ref unchanged
given: patch/foo is a guard candidate currently at sha_old
tests.when: a push updates patch/foo to sha_new
then: the report-status marks refs/heads/patch/foo ng with message 'branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url> instead'
the local ref for patch/foo is still sha_old
tests.pseudocode: r=push({patch/foo: sha_new}); assert r.status['refs/heads/patch/foo']=='ng branch is synced from origin; push to '+gitURL+' instead'; assert repoRef('patch/foo')==sha_old

tests.title: A rejected candidate ref does not prevent the packfile from being unpacked or other refs in the same push from being applied and reported ok
tests.when: a single push updates both patch/foo (new commit) and main (new commit) in one packfile
then: main's new commit object is unpacked into the object store
main's local ref is written to its new SHA and reported ok in the same report-status response
patch/foo is reported ng and left unchanged
tests.pseudocode: r=push({patch/foo:sha_a, main:sha_b}); assert r.status['refs/heads/main']=='ok'; assert repoRef('main')==sha_b; assert r.status['refs/heads/patch/foo']=='ng ...'; assert objectExists(sha_b)

tests.title: A forward attempt pushes the candidate ref to origin as a non-force push using ResolveCloneAuth credentials before the local ref is written
given: patch/foo is a guard candidate at sha_old locally
tests.when: a push updates patch/foo to sha_new
then: a non-force push of refs/heads/patch/foo:refs/heads/patch/foo is attempted against origin using workspace.ResolveCloneAuth's resolved credentials
the forward attempt completes before the local ref is written to sha_new
tests.pseudocode: spyPush=recordingRemote(); spyAuth=recordingResolveCloneAuth(); guard=NewPushGuardFunc(db,getVar,spyAuth); guard.forward('patch/foo', sha_new); assert spyPush.calls[0]=={remote:'origin', refspec:'refs/heads/patch/foo:refs/heads/patch/foo', force:false}; assert spyAuth.called

tests.title: A successful forward writes the local ref to the new SHA, reports ok, and releases the lock
given: the forward push to origin will succeed
tests.when: a push updates patch/foo to sha_new
then: the report-status marks refs/heads/patch/foo ok
the local ref for patch/foo equals sha_new
the fork's ref for patch/foo equals sha_new
the per-workspace lock is released once the push completes
tests.pseudocode: r=push({patch/foo:sha_new}); assert r.status['refs/heads/patch/foo']=='ok'; assert repoRef('patch/foo')==sha_new; assert forkRef('patch/foo')==sha_new; assert !wslock.isHeld(slug)

tests.title: A failed forward leaves the local ref unchanged and rejects the ref with the forward's own error text
given: the forward push to origin will fail with error 'non-fast-forward update'
tests.when: a push updates patch/foo to sha_new
then: the report-status marks refs/heads/patch/foo ng with message 'push to origin rejected: non-fast-forward update'
the local ref for patch/foo is unchanged from before the push
tests.pseudocode: r=push({patch/foo:sha_new}); assert r.status['refs/heads/patch/foo']=='ng push to origin rejected: non-fast-forward update'; assert repoRef('patch/foo')==sha_old

tests.title: A candidate ref whose per-workspace lock cannot be acquired is rejected with a busy message and no forward is attempted
given: the workspace's lock is already held by a concurrent operation
tests.when: a push updates patch/foo to sha_new
then: the report-status marks refs/heads/patch/foo ng with message 'workspace busy; try again'
no push to origin is attempted for patch/foo
tests.pseudocode: held,_=wslock.TryLock(slug); r=push({patch/foo:sha_new}); assert r.status['refs/heads/patch/foo']=='ng workspace busy; try again'; assert spyOriginPush.calls==0

tests.title: A forward failure or busy lock on one candidate ref never changes the accept/reject outcome of any other ref in the same push
given: two guard candidates patch/foo and patch/bar in the same push
tests.when: for any scenario where one candidate's lock acquisition or forward fails and the other candidate's forward succeeds, in either order
then: the succeeding candidate's ref is written and reported ok regardless of the other candidate's outcome
tests.pseudocode: for scenario in [busy_then_ok, ok_then_fail, fail_then_ok]: r=push(scenario); assert r.status[scenario.good_ref]=='ok'

tests.title: In hub-authoritative mode no pre-receive guard runs and every push is accepted exactly as before this spec
given: patch/foo is a registered, non-deleted patch branch
tests.when: a push updates patch/foo to sha_new
then: the report-status marks refs/heads/patch/foo ok
the local ref for patch/foo equals sha_new
no lock acquisition or origin push attempt occurs synchronously while accepting the push
tests.pseudocode: r=push({patch/foo:sha_new}); assert r.status['refs/heads/patch/foo']=='ok'; assert repoRef('patch/foo')==sha_new

tests.title: An accepted push in hub mode with mirroring enabled force-pushes every actually-updated registered patch branch to origin after the post-push hook runs
given: patch/foo is a registered active patch branch, main is the integration branch
tests.when: a push updates both patch/foo and main and completes
then: the mirror runs in the same goroutine as the post-push hook, after the hook finishes
a force-push of refs/heads/patch/foo:refs/heads/patch/foo is sent to origin using workspace.ResolveCloneAuth credentials while the per-workspace lock is held
main is not mirrored because it is the integration branch
tests.pseudocode: order=[]; hook=spyHook(order); mirror=NewMirrorFunc(db,getVar,spyAuth,order); r=push({patch/foo:sha1, main:sha2}); assert order==['hook','mirror']; assert spyForkPush.calls==[{ref:'patch/foo', force:true}]

tests.title: A busy lock during a mirror attempt skips that branch's mirror, logs it, and emits a hub.patch.mirror_failed audit event without affecting the push
given: the per-workspace lock is held by a concurrent operation when the mirror runs
tests.when: a push accepting an update to patch/foo triggers the mirror attempt
then: the push response already returned ok is unaffected

a hub.patch.mirror_failed audit event is recorded with EventType 'hub.patch.mirror_failed', ResourceType 'patch', ActorType 'system', Workspace equal to the slug, Metadata.branch_name='patch/foo', and a non-empty Metadata.error describing the busy lock
a log entry records the skip
tests.pseudocode: held,_=wslock.TryLock(slug); r=push({patch/foo:sha_new}); assert r.status=='ok'; ev=lastAuditEvent(); assert ev.EventType=='hub.patch.mirror_failed'; assert ev.Metadata['branch_name']=='patch/foo'; assert ev.Metadata['error']!=''

tests.title: A failed force-push during mirroring is logged and recorded as a hub.patch.mirror_failed audit event without affecting the push
given: the origin force-push for patch/foo will fail with 'connection reset'
tests.when: a push accepting an update to patch/foo triggers the mirror attempt
then: the push response already returned ok is unaffected
a hub.patch.mirror_failed audit event is recorded with Metadata.branch_name='patch/foo' and Metadata.error containing 'connection reset'
tests.pseudocode: r=push({patch/foo:sha_new}); assert r.status=='ok'; ev=lastAuditEvent(); assert ev.Metadata['error']=='connection reset'

tests.title: For any mirror attempt outcome, the push response and any triggered auto-rebuild are unaffected
tests.when: for any combination of mirror outcomes (success, lock busy, force-push failure) across the branches a push updates
then: the push's report-status and HTTP response are identical to the mirror-disabled case
the rebuild job triggered by AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH is enqueued exactly as without mirroring, with no additional delay
tests.pseudocode: for outcome in [success, busy, fail]: r=pushWithMirrorOutcome(outcome); assert r.status=='ok'; assert rebuildEnqueuedWithinSameLatency(r)

tests.title: internal/gitserver applies no guard when no pre-receive decision or mirror function is registered, demonstrating control is by registration alone
given: no pre-receive guard function or mirror function has been registered on gitserver
tests.when: a push to a candidate patch branch is made
then: the push is accepted exactly as before this spec (no guard applied), because the guard's behavior is entirely controlled by whether a function was registered, never by an internal/gitserver import of internal/carrypatch
tests.pseudocode: assert !sourceImports('internal/gitserver', 'internal/carrypatch'); r=push(patchFoo); assert r.status['refs/heads/patch/foo']=='ok'

tests.title: The registered pre-receive decision function is invoked with only the workspace's db, slug, trunk repo path, and candidate ref updates
given: a spy pre-receive decision function registered via the gitserver registration function
tests.when: a push containing one candidate ref and one non-candidate ref is made
then: the spy is called exactly once with (db, slug, trunkPath, candidateRefs) where candidateRefs contains only the guard candidate
gitserver uses only the spy's returned per-branch decision to accept or reject that branch
tests.pseudocode: spy=recordingGuard(); RegisterPushGuardFunc(spy); push({patchFoo, main}); assert spy.calls[0].args==(db, slug, trunkPath, ['patch/foo'])

tests.title: internal/carrypatch's production pre-receive decision function reads the workspace row, the variable store, and the patches table to compute its decision
given: a real database with a carry_patch workspace, PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin, PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN unset, and a patches row for patch/foo with status=active
tests.when: the carrypatch production pre-receive decision function is invoked directly with the candidate ref update for patch/foo
then: the returned decision is 'reject' carrying the origin-mode message, computed from the real workspace row, variable store, and patches table rather than from any caller-supplied override
tests.pseudocode: guard=carrypatch.NewPushGuardFunc(realDB, realGetVariable); d=guard(realDB, slug, trunkPath, [candidate('patch/foo')]); assert d['patch/foo'].reject==true

tests.title: A standard (non carry_patch) workspace's pushes never consult PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN or the patches table
given: a branch name that happens to match a row in the patches table
tests.when: a push updates that branch
then: the push is accepted exactly as before this spec
no PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN variable lookup and no patches table query is performed for this push
tests.pseudocode: spyVar=countingVarFunc(); spyDB=countingDB(); r=push(standardWs, branch); assert r.status=='ok'; assert spyVar.calls==0; assert spyDB.patchesQueryCount==0

tests.title: A push to a carry_patch workspace with no guard candidate applies no refusal, forward, or mirror behavior
given: a push touching only the integration branch and an unregistered branch
tests.when: the push is made
then: every ref is reported ok
no origin push, lock acquisition, or rejection occurs for any ref
tests.pseudocode: r=push({main:sha1, unregistered:sha2}); assert r.status['refs/heads/main']=='ok'; assert r.status['refs/heads/unregistered']=='ok'; assert spyOriginPush.calls==0

tests.title: The branches list passed to the post-push hook and the audit event's refs_updated/head_sha reflects only refs actually written by the push
given: a push updates patch/foo (rejected) and main (accepted)
tests.when: the push completes
then: the branches list passed to the post-push hook contains only 'main'
the hub.git.push audit event's refs_updated contains only refs/heads/main and head_sha is main's new SHA
tests.pseudocode: hookCalls=[]; postPushHook=recordHook(hookCalls); r=push({patch/foo:sha_a, main:sha_b}); assert hookCalls[0].branches==['main']; ev=lastAuditEvent(); assert ev.Metadata['refs_updated']==['refs/heads/main']; assert ev.Metadata['head_sha']==sha_b

tests.title: A rejected candidate ref is excluded from both the post-push hook's branch list and the mirror function's candidate branches
given: patch/foo is rejected under 04-REQ-3 in the same push that accepts main
tests.when: the push completes and the post-push hook and any mirror step run
then: the post-push hook does not consider patch/foo for auto-rebuild
no mirror attempt is made for patch/foo
tests.pseudocode: hookCalls=[]; postPushHook=recordHook(hookCalls); r=push({patch/foo:sha_a, main:sha_b}); assert 'patch/foo' not in hookCalls[0].branches; assert spyForkPush.calls==0

tests.title: The hub.git.push audit event's refs_updated and head_sha are computed from actually-written refs while every other field is unchanged
given: a push that partially rejects one candidate ref alongside an accepted ref
tests.when: the audit event is emitted after the push
then: refs_updated lists only the refs the push actually wrote
head_sha is the new SHA of an actually-written ref
EventType, ResourceType, Action, Workspace, ActorID, and ActorType are populated exactly as before this spec
tests.pseudocode: ev=lastAuditEvent(); assert ev.Metadata['refs_updated']==writtenRefs; assert ev.EventType=='hub.git.push'; assert ev.ResourceType=='workspace'; assert ev.Action=='push'

tests.title: A rejection under requirement 3 is logged at info level with the workspace slug, branch name, and pushing user's UserID
given: the pushing credential resolves to UserID 'user-1'
tests.when: a push to patch/foo is rejected
then: a log entry at info level is recorded containing the workspace slug, 'patch/foo', and 'user-1'
tests.pseudocode: logs=captureLogs(); push(patchFoo); entry=logs.find(level=='info'); assert entry.contains(slug); assert entry.contains('patch/foo'); assert entry.contains('user-1')

tests.title: A forward failure under requirement 4 is logged at warn level with the workspace slug, branch name, pushing user's UserID, and the forward error text
given: the forward push to origin fails with 'auth failed'
the pushing credential resolves to UserID 'user-1'
tests.when: a push to patch/foo is processed
then: a log entry at warn level is recorded containing the workspace slug, 'patch/foo', 'user-1', and 'auth failed'
tests.pseudocode: logs=captureLogs(); push(patchFoo); entry=logs.find(level=='warn'); assert entry.contains(slug); assert entry.contains('patch/foo'); assert entry.contains('user-1'); assert entry.contains('auth failed')

tests.title: For any rejection or forward-failure log entry, only the slug, branch, user, and (for forwards) error text fields are logged
tests.when: for any combination of rejection (04-REQ-3) and forward-failure (04-REQ-4) scenarios
then: the resulting log entry contains no stack trace marker and no packfile byte content
tests.pseudocode: for scenario in [reject, forward_fail]: entry=captureLog(scenario); assert !contains(entry,'goroutine '); assert !contains(entry, packfileBytes)

tests.title: docs/carry_patch_workflow.md's Configuration section documents PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN's origin-mode and hub-mode meanings
tests.when: the Configuration section is inspected
then: a PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN subsection exists, modelled on the AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH subsection, describing both the origin-mode reject-unless-forwarded meaning and the hub-mode best-effort-mirror meaning
tests.pseudocode: doc=readFile('docs/carry_patch_workflow.md'); assert doc.contains('PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN'); assert doc.section('Configuration').contains('reject'); assert doc.section('Configuration').contains('mirror')

tests.title: docs/carry_patch_workflow.md's How it works / Auto-rebuild on push area describes the pre-receive refusal, forward, and mirror including the exact rejection message
tests.when: the How it works section is inspected
then: it describes the pre-receive refusal and forward and the mirror
it contains the exact string 'branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url> instead'
tests.pseudocode: doc=readFile('docs/carry_patch_workflow.md'); assert doc.contains('branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url> instead')

tests.title: docs/examples/AGENTS_carry_patch.md's Step 4 tells the agent to check PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE before pushing and push to the correct remote
tests.when: Step 4 ('Push to the Hub') is inspected
then: it instructs the agent to check PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE before pushing
it instructs pushing to the hub's git server in hub mode
it instructs pushing directly to the fork's own URL in origin mode unless PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN=true
tests.pseudocode: doc=readFile('docs/examples/AGENTS_carry_patch.md'); step4=doc.section('Push to the Hub'); assert step4.contains('PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE'); assert step4.contains('PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN')

tests.title: A developer's direct push to a fork-synced patch branch through the running hub git server is refused end to end
given: a running hub with a real database and a real trunk git repository
a carry_patch workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin and PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN unset
a registered active patch branch patch/foo
tests.when: a real git push (via git-receive-pack over the hub's git smart HTTP endpoint) attempts to update patch/foo
then: the client receives an ng status for refs/heads/patch/foo carrying the fork-push message
the workspace's local ref for patch/foo is unchanged
an info-level log entry recording the rejection is produced

tests.title: A forwarded push to a fork-synced patch branch is accepted locally only after succeeding against the fork, and triggers an auto-rebuild
given: a running hub with a real database, a real trunk git repository, and a real fork (a local bare repo standing in for origin)
a registered active patch branch patch/foo
tests.when: a real git push updates patch/foo
then: the fork's ref for patch/foo equals the new SHA before the local ref is written
the client receives ok for refs/heads/patch/foo
the local ref equals the new SHA
a rebuild job is enqueued for the workspace

tests.title: An accepted hub-authoritative push is best-effort mirrored to a real fork without affecting the push or its rebuild
given: a running hub with a real database, a real trunk git repository, and a real fork (a local bare repo standing in for origin)
a registered active patch branch patch/foo
tests.when: a real git push updates patch/foo
then: the client receives ok for refs/heads/patch/foo immediately
the local ref is updated
the auto-rebuild job is enqueued without waiting for the mirror
the fork's ref for patch/foo is eventually force-pushed to match the new SHA

tests.title: A single push updating both a fork-synced patch branch and the integration branch is partially accepted with corrected audit metadata and no rebuild for the rejected branch
given: a running hub with a real database and a real trunk git repository
a registered active patch branch patch/foo and integration branch main
tests.when: a single real git push updates both patch/foo and main
then: the client receives ng for refs/heads/patch/foo and ok for refs/heads/main in the same report-status response
main's local ref is updated and patch/foo's is unchanged
the hub.git.push audit event's refs_updated contains only refs/heads/main and head_sha is main's new SHA
no rebuild job referencing patch/foo is enqueued from this push
